mission_assessment.heart: authorized peer-to-peer folder convergence under evidence-bound local truth
mission_assessment.rev0697_role: turn the persisted workorder lifecycle into a non-mutating scheduler read model before adding daemon mutation

audit_refactor_target: resume-transfer workorder lifecycle read model and daemon queue-selection boundary
audit_findings: Rev0696 stored enough facts to recover safely, but daemon queue selection would still have required ad hoc SQL or policy duplication.
Ownership must require both worker_id and worker_lease_id; matching worker names alone are not runnable evidence.
Expired claims require retry_at_epoch and attempt-cap interpretation before any reclaim/abandon mutator should run.
Terminal abandoned/quarantined rows should remain review facts in the selector, not be silently mixed into ordinary runnable work.
Completed rows should remain hidden from ordinary scheduling and only appear when explicitly requested for audit.
behavioral_invariants_added: The selector opens the checkpoint database read-only and does not mutate workorder rows or event tables.
Rows are considered owned only when both worker_id and worker_lease_id match the selector options.
Expired rows whose retry_at_epoch is in the future are cooling down, not reclaim-ready.
Retry-open expired rows at max_workorder_claim_attempts are abandon-ready, not reclaim-ready.
Abandoned and quarantined rows are terminal review facts until a separate reset operation deliberately reopens them.
Completed rows are ignored by default and exposed only when include_completed_workorders is true.
